newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel still hopes for tax deal with SPD by Easter.
newsitem.headline: Waigel still hopes for tax deal with SPD by Easter.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that a cross-party compromise on German tax reforms was still possible by Easter if the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) returned to the negotiating table.

But Waigel criticised the SPD's decision to pull out of a meeting on Saturday to discuss his proposals to cut 30 billion marks in taxes in protest at government plans to more than halve subsidies to Germany's loss-making coal mines.
"We have not slammed the door," Waigel told reporters.

Waigel added that the issues of coal and taxes were not related. He repeated an ultimatum he issued at the weekend to introduce tax legislation to parliament this Friday if the SPD does not rejoin the tax talks.
"The country cannot allow itself to become dependent on the whims of the SPD," he said.
Waigel also said that the government, which wants to cut federal coal aid to 3.8 billion marks a year by 2005 from nine billion marks this year, had already "gone a long way" to reach a consensus.
The SPD's leadership was meeting on Monday to decide whether to rejoin the tax talks.
